title: Distinct source years raised the Arctic three-river peak contrast from 1.73% to 1.94% in 1980-2011
abstract: We tested whether repeated source-year labels change a reference for summed river-flow peaks. We used 31 certified years at Ob, Yenisey and Lena gauges from ArcticGRO v20261104. The same-year mean seven-day peak exceeded an all-triple reference by 1.73%. A reference with three distinct source years gave 1.94%. The contrast rose by 483 cubic metres per second, or 11.34%. An exact collision identity explains the change. Under independent paired year vectors, the distinct-year reference is unbiased for a population product of marginal distributions. Exact enumeration of a synthetic example confirms the distinction. The earlier all-triple reference remains valid for its conditional permutation target. A three-year block interval for the new contrast was 1344 to 8209 cubic metres per second, with limited coverage assurance. Short selected records, serial dependence, regulation, gauge error and absent coast travel limit inference. No physical cause or ocean response is established. Code, aggregate evidence, hashes and retrieval steps are included; source records remain external.

display.caption: Gauge-flow peak contrasts with conditional three-year block intervals, and a synthetic population-reference check.
